premises.text: Mass retail cannot stock prestige niche makeup colors because volume-driven supply chains limit assortment, while prestige stores are expensive
premises.evidence_span: Walmart can't offer you all the colors that expensive prestige stores can, like Sephora. Why? Supply chain

premises.text: A desktop inkjet-like printer turns any digital image or hex color into wearable cosmetics using FDA-compliant ink and substrates
premises.evidence_span: Mink is a desktop printer that prints makeup. It can take any image and instantly transform it into a wearable color cosmetic

premises.text: Hardware retails around $300 with commodity-priced consumables so colors stay accessible at home
premises.evidence_span: I'm going to retail this for about $300 initially. And the ink and the substrates are going to be commodity priced

premises.text: Initial customers are girls ages 13–21 who are still experimenting and learn makeup online
premises.evidence_span: My initial target market, they're girls, ages 13 to 21. They have not formed any habits yet

premises.text: An open developer path extends printing beyond eyeshadow to other cosmetic formats from web images
premises.evidence_span: We're printing eyeshadow right now, but this is basically gonna be able to print lipsticks, powders, creams, foundations, et cetera

value.text: Prestige-level color selection with mass convenience at home from any digital color
value.evidence_span: It gives you the selection of prestige and it combines it with the convenience of mass

secondary_value.text: Girls control their own definition of beauty rather than corporations
secondary_value.evidence_span: The definition of beauty is something that they should be able to control, not our corporations

causal_links.evidence_span: if you want like the cool niche colors, you have to go to expensive Sephora
turning any phone, laptop, or camera into an endless beauty aisle
